title: Student identity is directly disclosed with the submission
description: The student sends a student identifier together with the assignment file, course, and submission timestamp. This directly reveals the submitter's identity to the receiving system as part of the flow.
assumptions: The student id is unique or reasonably attributable to a specific student.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement from generic LINDDUN identity-disclosure categorization; exact sub-node may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Submission metadata can link multiple actions by the same student
description: Data in transit includes student id, course, and submission timestamp. Together these attributes enable linking this submission to the student's other portal activities or submissions, especially if observed across sessions or flows.
assumptions: An observer of the flow, intermediary, or logging component can access the transmitted metadata.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree sub-node may differ depending on whether the methodology distinguishes linkability via identifiers versus contextual metadata.

title: In-transit data reveals student identity and academic activity
description: The transmitted payload contains a student id and assignment-related content plus course and timestamp metadata. If exposed in transit, it reveals both who the student is and what academic activity they are performing.
assumptions: Transport protection may be absent, weak, terminated early, or logs/monitoring systems may expose payload or metadata.
uncertainty_note: Applies strongly if transport or intermediary logging exposes payload/metadata; if end-to-end protections are robust, likelihood is lower.

title: Portal can detect the student's assignment-submission behavior
description: By receiving the assignment file, student id, course, and precise submission timestamp, the portal can observe that the student is enrolled in a course and detect when and how often they submit work. This creates observability of academic behavior at the destination.
assumptions: The portal stores or processes the received submission metadata in a way that makes the behavior observable to operators or internal components.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; exact detectability sub-node depends on the threat-tree version.

title: Submission data may be used beyond the student's expectations
description: The destination receives rich content and metadata that could be reused for secondary purposes, such as plagiarism analytics, performance profiling, retention beyond grading needs, or sharing with other university functions, without the student's clear understanding.
assumptions: The portal or its operators have discretion to repurpose or retain submissions beyond the immediate grading function.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible unawareness threat at the destination, but applicability depends on whether notice and consent mechanisms are already in place.

title: Collection of assignment content and detailed metadata may exceed necessity
description: The portal receives a work file, student id, course, and exact submission timestamp. If all of these fields, especially precise timestamps or persistent identifiers, are not strictly necessary for the submission purpose, the flow may violate data-minimization or purpose-limitation expectations.
assumptions: Some received attributes may be more detailed than required for accepting and grading the assignment.
uncertainty_note: This depends on the portal's purpose and institutional policy; exact non-compliance basis is context-dependent.

title: Portal shares identified student data with grading service
description: The portal forwards student id together with course and requesting role to the assignment & grading service. This is processing and disclosure of identified data, enabling the recipient to directly associate the request with a specific student.
assumptions: Student id is a stable identifier for an individual student and is not immediately transformed into an anonymous token before transmission.

title: Data flow contains a unique student identifier
description: The transmitted payload includes student id, which is a unique reference to the data subject. Anyone able to observe or access the flow can identify the student associated with the submission or grading request.
assumptions: The student id is unique within the institution and visible in the transmitted message or its metadata.

title: Submission and grading requests can link a student's activities across courses or assignments
description: Because the same student id is sent alongside course information and file reference, observations of this flow can be linked over time to build a profile of a student's submissions, courses, and grading-related interactions.
assumptions: The same student id is reused across requests and the observer can correlate multiple messages on this flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree node citation is based on general LINDDUN linkability structure; exact subnode may vary.

title: Received submission/grading requests may create attributable evidence of a student's actions
description: By receiving student id, course, file reference, and requesting role, the grading service may retain evidence that a particular student submitted or requested grading activity. This can reduce the student's ability to deny involvement in that action.
assumptions: The grading service logs or stores the request with sufficient integrity and attribution to be used as evidence later.
uncertainty_note: Exact non-repudiation subnode is approximate because the retrieved context gives the threat type but not a specific tree-node breakdown.

title: Grading service learns details about a student's academic activity
description: On receipt, the assignment & grading service learns the student's identity, course enrollment context, file reference, and role associated with the request. This reveals personal information about the student's academic participation beyond the minimum fact that a request exists.
assumptions: These attributes are personal data in context and are available to the service and potentially its operators.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure subnode is approximate because no specific disclosure node was provided in the retrieved context.

title: Excessive disclosure when storing assignment submission metadata
description: The grading service stores the submitted assignment together with student id, course, and submission time. If all of these attributes are not strictly necessary for the storage purpose, the act of sending them to the data store constitutes avoidable disclosure of personal data beyond data minimization.
assumptions: Assumes at least one of the transmitted attributes is not strictly required for assignment storage or later grading/audit purposes.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for explicit/avoidable disclosure under data minimization; exact sub-node may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Over-retention or unnecessary storage of identifiable submission data
description: On receipt, the assignment store may retain the assignment file and associated student id, course, and precise submission time in identifiable form longer than necessary or at greater granularity than needed, creating avoidable disclosure risk through stored personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the data store persists the data and that retention/granularity controls are not already constrained elsewhere in the design.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree sub-node may differ depending on whether the repository distinguishes unnecessary storage, excessive granularity, or retention under separate Dd branches.

title: Stored submission records enable linkage across assignments or courses
description: Because the store receives student id together with course and submission time, records can be linked across multiple submissions, courses, or time periods to build a broader profile of a student's behavior and academic activity.
assumptions: Assumes DS1 stores multiple records over time and permits correlation using stable identifiers or timestamps.
uncertainty_note: Applicable linkage threat is clear, but the exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node id is estimated from general linkage taxonomy.

title: Student identity is directly inferable from stored submission data
description: The assignment store receives a direct student identifier alongside the submission, making the data attributable to a specific student. If identifiable storage is not necessary for all downstream purposes, the destination creates an identifiability threat.
assumptions: Assumes student id is a direct identifier and that some storage or processing purposes could be fulfilled with a less identifiable representation.
uncertainty_note: Threat applicability is strong; exact sub-node id is best-effort due to limited retrieved tree detail.

title: Submission metadata reveals student activity patterns
description: The combination of course and submission time can reveal when a student was active, whether they submitted close to deadlines, and potentially aspects of workload or behavior. Storing these attributes enables inference of personal patterns beyond the assignment content itself.
assumptions: Assumes submission timestamps are stored with sufficient precision and can be queried or analyzed.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible detectability/inference-style privacy threat; exact classification and sub-node may vary depending on the project's interpretation of D versus I/L.

title: Teacher submits identified account credentials and role context
description: When logging in and requesting the review queue, the teacher provides identified data such as username/email and implicitly their teacher role and course affiliation. The act of sharing this identified data creates an identifying threat if more identity information than necessary is sent for this request.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request includes direct identifiers or stable account identifiers rather than fully anonymous or pairwise pseudonymous credentials.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 is directly supported by the retrieved context; exact credential fields are inferred from the flow description.

title: Request metadata can link teacher activity across sessions
description: Metadata on the flow, such as stable account identifiers, session identifiers, IP address, timing, and repeated requests for course review queues, can enable linking multiple actions and sessions to the same teacher.
assumptions: Assumes ordinary web-app transport exposes stable metadata to intermediaries, logs, or network observers, even if payload contents are protected.
uncertainty_note: Exact L threat-tree subnode may vary; using L.1 as best judgement because retrieved context did not include linking nodes.

title: Data in transit may identify the teacher
description: The login and queue-request flow may contain direct or indirect identifiers in transit, such as username, email address, employee ID, session token tied to an account, or course identifiers that single out the teacher.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are present in headers, parameters, cookies, or message body.
uncertainty_note: I.1.1 is a close fit for identified data, though the exact in-transit fields are inferred.

title: Portal learns the teacher's review activity and course workload
description: By receiving the login and queue request, the portal can observe that this teacher is active, which courses they are reviewing, and when they access grading queues. This creates detectability of the teacher's behavior and workload patterns.
assumptions: Assumes the portal logs requests and associates them with teacher accounts and course context.
uncertainty_note: Exact D subnode is best judgement because no detectability node was provided in the retrieved context.

title: Portal may process login/request data without sufficient transparency
description: If the portal does not clearly inform teachers how login events, queue requests, access logs, and course-review activity are collected, retained, and used, the processing lacks adequate transparency and awareness.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or just-in-time explanations for teacher activity logging may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Exact Nc subnode is best judgement because the retrieved context did not include non-compliance tree details.

title: Excessive disclosure of student submission data to teacher
description: The portal may disclose more personal data than necessary when presenting submissions to the teacher, such as full student names, detailed timestamps, or full work content where only limited information is needed for the teacher's task. This creates a disclosure risk because the source process chooses what data to share.
assumptions: Assumes some displayed fields may exceed what is necessary for the teacher's legitimate educational purpose, or may be visible beyond the relevant class/context.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on whether the teacher is authorized for all displayed students and whether data minimization has been applied.

title: Identifiability of students in transit
description: The flow contains direct identifiers such as student names alongside submission content and times, making individual students identifiable from the transmitted data if the flow is observed or logged.
assumptions: Assumes the transmitted payload or related transport/logging metadata can be accessed by unauthorized parties or intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: If strong transport protection and strict logging controls are in place, practical exploitability is reduced.

title: Linkability of student activity across submissions
description: Combining student names, work content, and submission times in the same flow enables linking multiple submissions and activity patterns to the same student over time.
assumptions: Assumes repeated observations of this flow, or retained logs/telemetry, allow correlation across sessions or assignments.
uncertainty_note: I am confident on the threat type, but the exact tree node is a best-judgment generic linkability node.

title: Disclosure through interception or verbose transport/logging
description: Because the flow carries student names, submission content, and timestamps, interception of the transmission or exposure through browser, proxy, or application logs could reveal confidential student information.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate transport security, caching, or logging minimization.
uncertainty_note: Likelihood depends strongly on deployment controls such as TLS, cache headers, and log redaction.

title: Unauthorized onward disclosure by teacher
description: Once received, the teacher could further disclose student submissions, names, or timing information to unauthorized parties, for example by screenshots, downloads, sharing, or displaying them in an inappropriate context.
assumptions: Assumes the teacher interface permits viewing/exporting/capturing data and that policy or technical controls may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine destination-side privacy threat, though actual likelihood depends on organizational controls and teacher role boundaries.

title: Lack of transparency to students about teacher access
description: Students may not be adequately informed that their names, work content, and submission times are displayed to teachers, under what circumstances, and for what purposes. This undermines transparency and awareness regarding processing at the recipient side.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices, in-product notices, or educational policies do not clearly explain this recipient access.
uncertainty_note: This may be mitigated if the educational context and notices already make teacher access obvious and well documented.

title: Teacher can later deny having submitted or authored a grade/feedback entry
description: If the submission of grade, feedback text, student id, and grader id is not strongly bound to the authenticated teacher and time of submission, the teacher may plausibly deny having entered or changed the assessment. This creates a privacy-relevant repudiation risk around accountability for personal data processing.
assumptions: Assumes the portal may lack strong authentication binding, tamper-evident audit logs, or explicit confirmation of submission.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Teacher identity or student identity may be exposed in transit
description: The flow carries direct identifiers and assessment content: student id, grader id, grade, and written feedback. If the transmission channel is observable or insufficiently protected, an attacker could identify the student and teacher associated with a specific assessment event.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection or endpoint authenticity may be absent, weak, or misconfigured.

title: Sensitive academic performance data may be disclosed in transit
description: Grades and written feedback are personal data about a student's academic performance and may also reveal information about the teacher's evaluation. Interception or unintended exposure of this flow would disclose confidential educational information.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow could be intercepted, logged, or exposed through insecure transport or intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate; context did not provide detailed disclosure subnodes.

title: Portal can link grading actions across students and assignments to build teacher and student profiles
description: On receipt, the web app can associate grader id, student id, grade, feedback text, assignment context, and timestamps. This enables linking multiple grading events over time, revealing patterns about a teacher's behavior and a student's performance history beyond the immediate purpose of recording one grade.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores or analyzes submissions across multiple events and contexts.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; linkage is clearly applicable at the destination, but the exact subnode is not available in the provided context.

title: Portal can identify the teacher and student from submitted grading data

title: Portal may disclose grades and feedback to unauthorized internal users or downstream components
description: Once received, the process may store, display, or forward grade and feedback data in ways that expose student performance information or teacher comments to parties without a legitimate need to know.

title: Teacher may be unaware of secondary uses or retention of submitted grading data
description: After receipt, the portal may retain grades and feedback, use them for analytics, quality monitoring, model training, or broader reporting without making these uses sufficiently transparent to the teacher or affected student. This creates an unawareness threat regarding how the submitted personal data is processed.

uncertainty_note: Exact node id is approximate.

title: Portal may process grading data without an appropriate legal basis, policy basis, or educational-governance constraint
description: The destination receives identifiable student performance data and teacher-authored feedback. If the portal processes, retains, or repurposes this data beyond authorized educational purposes or contrary to institutional policy or applicable privacy law, the flow contributes to non-compliance.

title: Direct identification of student in stored grade record
description: The grading service writes a grade record containing a student identifier together with course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp. By sending a directly identifying student id into persistent storage, the source causes the student to be identifiable from this record.

title: Disclosure of sensitive academic performance data in storage

title: Non-compliance risk from storing identifiable grade records

Persisting student id, grades, feedback, grader id, and timestamps can create non-compliance risk if storage, access, retention, or purpose limitation requirements are not met.

uncertainty_note: Applicable obligations depend on jurisdiction and institution; tree node id is approximate.

title: Student provides identified request data

assumptions: Assumes the grades portal requires authenticated access and the request contains direct or indirect identifiers tied to a student account.

title: Request metadata can identify the student in transit

description: Multiple requests from the same student to view grades and feedback can be linked together through stable identifiers in transit, such as session cookies, account IDs, IP address patterns, or browser fingerprints, allowing correlation of the student's interactions over time.

title: Disclosure of grades or feedback during transmission

description: The student may not be sufficiently informed about what grade-related data is shown, how current it is, whether feedback is final, or how long it remains accessible, undermining transparency.

description: If the student-facing view includes unnecessary personal data, third-party data, or feedback not intended for student access, the disclosure may violate privacy obligations or educational data handling policies.
